label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. They appear to be psychologically well-adjusted, with UCLA-8 loneliness scores, PHQ-9 depression scores, and GAD-7 anxiety scores all well below typical thresholds of concern. The cluster is moderately sized (n=115), suggesting a stable and replicable subgroup.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Very low loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.78), indicating strong social connectedness
Minimal depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.25), well below clinical screening thresholds
Near-floor anxiety levels (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.04), suggesting negligible anxiety burden
Moderate and controlled screen/internet use (1–3 hours daily)
Higher educational attainment, which may serve as a protective factor
tone: Calm, stable, and socially connected — reflecting a low-distress, well-functioning profile

label: Lonely, Distressed High-Screen-Time Graduate Women
summary: This profile captures highly educated women who spend more than five hours daily on screens and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their UCLA-8 loneliness scores (mean ≈ 1.69), PHQ-9 depression scores (mean ≈ 1.68), and GAD-7 anxiety scores (mean ≈ 2.15) are all in the higher range, suggesting a co-occurring pattern of psychological distress. The profile comprises 178 respondents from the training sample.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily screen time exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness as measured by UCLA-8 (mean ≈ 1.69)
Notably high anxiety symptoms on GAD-7 (mean ≈ 2.15)
Extended daily screen time of more than 5 hours
Co-occurrence of loneliness, depression, and anxiety indicators
tone: Concerned and empathetic; clinically attentive to compounding psychological distress

label: Well-Adjusted Female Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report consistently low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. With UCLA-8 loneliness scores averaging around 1.22, PHQ-9 depression scores near 0.82, and GAD-7 anxiety scores near 0.83, these individuals fall well below clinical thresholds across all three psychological distress measures, suggesting generally positive mental well-being.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily screen/social media use
behavior_markers: Reports minimal feelings of loneliness or social isolation
Demonstrates low anxiety levels well below clinical concern
Maintains moderate and bounded screen or social media use (1–3 hours daily)
Psychological distress scores consistently cluster near the low end of all three scales
tone: Calm, emotionally stable, and psychologically resilient
